sentences: Credit utilization, the share of the credit limit in use, is the most important driver of default risk, accounting for about 28% of the model's importance, and risk rises strongly as utilization increases.
The number of past delinquencies is the second most important driver, accounting for about 17% of importance, and risk jumps when an applicant has at least one past delinquency.
The effect of credit utilization grows with the number of past delinquencies, and the pair together accounts for about 20% of the model's importance.
Income and the length of credit history have moderate effects, with risk falling as either rises.
The debt-to-income ratio has a weak to moderate effect, with risk rising as it increases.
Recent credit inquiries have at most a weak effect, while the number of dependents, months at the current address and age hardly matter.
The data do not settle whether the length of credit history and credit utilization interact.
